definition: A variant of the MNIST benchmark with rotated digits, used to evaluate rotation invariance and data augmentation.
details: A variant of the MNIST benchmark with rotated digits, used to evaluate rotation invariance and data augmentation.

explainer.lead: Rotated MNIST is a variant of the MNIST digit benchmark in which the digits are rotated. It is used to test rotation invariance and the effect of data augmentation.

tiers.eli5: It's the classic handwritten-digit dataset, but the numbers are tilted at different angles so a model has to recognise a '7' even when it's sideways.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to compare models trained with and without rotated training examples or rotation-invariant architectures. A pitfall is testing on rotations never seen in training, which measures generalization rather than invariance.
tiers.paperLevel: The dataset keeps MNIST's 28x28 grayscale digit images and labels but applies rotation transforms to them; accuracy is reported as standard classification accuracy, and results depend heavily on the rotation range used.

explainer.example: A classifier trained only on upright digits scores poorly on digits rotated 90 degrees, while the same model trained with augmented rotations recovers much of its accuracy.
